get.description: Returns the resolved price for a product using the V2 pricing engine. Optionally pass a customer code for customer-specific pricing (contracts, price lists). The price is decided by ENTITLEMENT PRECEDENCE, not by which source is cheapest: the customer's own contract governs, then a contract held through their buying group, then their price list, then the standard price — the first of those that covers the product wins, whether it sits below the standard price or above it. A promotion is applied only where it improves on that entitled price. Without a customerCode the entitled price is the standard price, and only promotions scoped to all customers can improve on it. `resolvedPrice` is therefore frequently not the lowest price any source offers, and `discountPct` is negative where an entitlement marks the customer up.

discountPct.description: Effective discount off the standard price, in percent. NEGATIVE when the resolved price is above standard — an entitlement that marks a customer up is authoritative, so a markup is reported as a negative discount rather than as zero.

info.title: JRNY Integration API
info.description: REST API for external integrations with the JRNY ERP platform. Supports machine-to-machine (M2M) authentication via bearer tokens, quotation creation, entity discovery, API key management, and webhook subscriptions. All endpoints are rate-limited and return structured error responses with X-Request-Id tracing.

IntegrationBearerAuth.description: Integration API key obtained from the JRNY admin panel. Provide via the Authorization header: Bearer <api-key>

stockCode.description: Stock code / SKU of the product

uom.description: Unit of measure code. Must be a unit this product can be transacted in — one this API's product endpoint reports in `sellingUom` or on the product's UOM ladder — or the line is refused. Omit it and the server resolves the unit from the product master (its default selling unit, else the unit it is stocked in); it never assumes one. No `example` is given on purpose: a sample unit here reads as a default, and there is no default — the answer belongs to the product.

unitPrice.description: Unit price (excl. VAT). Defaults to pricing engine resolution if omitted

addressCode.description: Reference to an existing address code on the customer. Mutually exclusive with inline address fields

suburb.description: Suburb — couriers route on suburb + postal code

lines.description: Quotation line items (at least one required)

deliveryAddress.description: Delivery address. Use addressCode to reference an existing customer address, or provide inline fields (addressLine1, city, etc.). Cannot mix both modes

externalReference.description: External reference number from the calling system

portalCode.description: Which portal sent this order (e.g. SHOPRITE). The portal's own order number goes in externalReference. Trimmed; blank means none. When both are sent, the pair identifies the portal order: a second create with the same portalCode and externalReference returns 409 DUPLICATE_PORTAL_ORDER naming the existing document. Matched exactly (case-sensitive). Returned as portalCode on every quotation and sales order read, and filterable with ?portalCode=.

notes.description: Free-text notes to include on the quotation

quotationDate.description: Quotation date (ISO 8601). Defaults to today if omitted

validUntil.description: Valid-until date (ISO 8601). Defaults to quotationDate + customer payment term days

deliveryDate.description: Required delivery date (ISO 8601). Required when autoConfirm is true

autoConvert.description: Auto-convert quotation to a sales order after creation. Defaults to false

autoConfirm.description: Auto-confirm the resulting sales order (requires autoConvert=true and deliveryDate). Defaults to false

tax.description: A numeric string. Named `tax` on sales documents, `vat` on POs.

externalReference.description: The external system's own reference, echoed back. ?externalRef= filters the list on it, which is how an integration finds the quotation it created without storing our id.

portalCode.description: Which portal sent the quotation (e.g. SHOPRITE); null when none was sent. ?portalCode= filters the list on it.

cursor.description:
Pass back as ?cursor= for the next page; null on the last page. THE ENCODING VARIES BY ENDPOINT and a client must treat it as opaque — it is not one scheme:
  • customers, products, price-lists — a BASE64-ENCODED OFFSET. Offset pagination, so rows inserted mid-scan shift the window and a row can be seen twice or skipped.
  • invoices, credit notes, debit notes, payments, vendors, purchase orders, GRNs, supplier invoices, quotations, sales orders — a RAW ROW ID. The cursor row is re-read for its (createdAt, id) and the page compares COMPOUND on that pair, not createdAt alone, so rows sharing a createdAt are still ordered deterministically and nothing straddles a page boundary. The default order is DESCENDING; with ?apiDelivery= on invoices, credit notes and debit notes it runs ASCENDING instead (oldest first, R1), so the same cursor value is read in whichever direction that endpoint is paging. If the cursor row no longer exists (deleted, or from another entity), the next page is a 400, never a silent restart from the beginning.
  • dispatch notes — a RAW DISPATCH NUMBER, paged with `>`, ASCENDING. The only other ascending list in the API.

hasMore.description: Whether another page exists. AUTHORITATIVE — prefer it over testing `cursor !== null`, and over `data.length === limit`.

poReference.description: The customer's purchase-order reference: customerPoNumber, or — for an order that predates that column — the legacy externalReference. ?poReference= filters the list on either column.

customerPoNumber.description: The customer's PO number as stored on the order (customer_po_number).

externalReference.description: The integration's own document reference (externalReference), as sent.

portalCode.description: Which portal sent the order — copied from its quotation, or sent on a direct create; null otherwise. ?portalCode= filters the list on it.

fulfillmentSummary.description: How far the order has been fulfilled, summarised. Returned WITH the order so an integration polling order status does not need the separate fulfilment call.

dispatches.description: Dispatches, with waybill and courier status where booked.

invoices.description: Invoices raised from those dispatches. THE THREE ARRAYS ARE INDEPENDENT — an order can have dispatches with no invoice (dispatched, not yet invoiced), so their lengths do not have to agree.

lineNumber.description: The pick line's own number (1, 2, 3… over the lines this pick carries; one order line can split into several pick lines across bins).

orderLineNumber.description: The sales order line this pick line fulfils; null if the link is missing.

quantity.description: Quantity to pick, in the stocking unit (uom).

binCode.description: The bin to pick from; null when none was resolved.

warehouseCode.description: The pick's warehouse code; null when the order's branch resolved none.

fingerprint.description: A short non-secret identifier for the key, safe to display and log. THIS IS NOT THE TOKEN — the token itself is returned exactly once, at creation or rotation, and is not stored in retrievable form.

scopes.description: Granted scopes. Normalised to [] when the column is null.

rateLimit.description: Requests per window. NULL MEANS NO EXPLICIT LIMIT on the key, not a limit of zero.

serviceUserId.description: The key's service identity (a core.users id of kind 'integration'; equals the key id). Every request made with this key is recorded as this user. Null only for a key the migration-3117 backfill has not reached — its requests act as createdBy.

identityName.description: The name the audit trail and the created / confirmed by fields show for this key. Follows the key display name.

lastUsedAt.description: Null means the key has never been used — useful for spotting keys issued and forgotten.

revokedAt.description: Non-null means the key is revoked and will not authenticate.

isRotating.description: Computed, not stored: rotationExpiresAt is in the future AND the key is not revoked. While true, BOTH the old and the new token authenticate — that is the point of the grace period, and it is the window in which a leaked old token still works.

rotationExpiresAt.description: When the old token stops working. Null when no rotation is in progress.

keys.description: Wrapped under `keys`, not `data`, and with no total.

displayName.description: Human-readable label for the API key (e.g. "JRNYFLW Production Key")

scopes.description: List of integration permission codes this key is allowed to use. Empty array (default) means unrestricted — all scopes allowed. EXCEPT explicit-grant scopes (fulfilment.write — generate picks), which a key holds only when they are listed. Listing only explicit-grant scopes leaves the key otherwise unrestricted.

rateLimit.description: Per-key rate limit in requests per minute. Default: 60.

token.description: THE PLAINTEXT API KEY, RETURNED EXACTLY ONCE. It is not stored in retrievable form, so it cannot be fetched again from any endpoint — a caller that does not capture it here must rotate the key to get a new one. Do not log it.

fingerprint.description: The non-secret identifier for this key, safe to store and display.

serviceUserId.description: The key's service identity (a core.users id of kind 'integration'; equals the key id). Every request made with this key is recorded as this user. Null only for a key the migration-3117 backfill has not reached — its requests act as createdBy.

identityName.description: The name the audit trail and the created / confirmed by fields show for this key. Follows the key display name.

displayName.description: Updated human-readable label for the API key

scopes.description: Updated list of integration permission codes. Empty array means unrestricted — all scopes allowed. EXCEPT explicit-grant scopes (fulfilment.write — generate picks), which a key holds only when they are listed. Listing only explicit-grant scopes leaves the key otherwise unrestricted.

rateLimit.description: Updated per-key rate limit in requests per minute.

gracePeriodHours.description: Grace period in hours during which both old and new tokens are valid

newToken.description: THE NEW PLAINTEXT KEY, RETURNED EXACTLY ONCE, with the same caveats as on creation.

gracePeriodHours.description: How long the OLD token keeps working alongside the new one. During this window both authenticate.

rotationExpiresAt.description: When the old token stops working.

subscriptions.description: Wrapped under `subscriptions`, not `data`, and with no total. Empty in dev.

domain.description: The domain the event belongs to, e.g. 'sales'.

eventTypes.description: The subscribable event catalogue — a frozen constant, not a query, so it is the authoritative list of what a subscription may ask for. 11 events at the time of writing.
The event types this subscription receives. See GET /webhooks/event-types.

isActive.description: FALSE MEANS EVENTS ARE SILENTLY NOT DELIVERED. Nothing queues them for later — a disabled subscription misses everything that happens while it is off.

url.description: URL to deliver webhook events to. Must be HTTPS (except localhost for development).

events.description: Array of event types to subscribe to.

url.description: Updated URL to deliver webhook events to. Must be HTTPS (except localhost for development).

events.description: Updated array of event types to subscribe to.

isActive.description: Whether this subscription is active and should receive events.

success.description: Whether the endpoint accepted the delivery. FALSE IS A NORMAL OUTCOME here — this is a diagnostic call against a customer-supplied URL, so a failure is information, not an error condition, and the request itself still returns 200.

statusCode.description: The receiving endpoint's HTTP status. Null when no response was received at all.

samplePayload.description: The payload that was sent. Present on sendTestEvent (which delivers a representative event body) and absent on sendTestPing, which sends only a ping.

totalCalls24h.description: API calls in the last 24 hours.

successRate24h.description: Percentage of those calls that succeeded. 0 when there were no calls, which reads the same as "everything failed" — check totalCalls24h first.

webhookSuccessRate24h.description: Webhook delivery success rate over the same window. Same 0 caveat.

calls.description: Recent API calls, newest first. Empty in dev.

totalCount.description: The TRUE total from a count query, not the page size.

failed.description: Deliveries that failed but may still be retried.

deadLetter.description: Deliveries that exhausted their retries. THIS IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS — a failed delivery may recover, a dead-lettered one will not without intervention.

chart.description: One entry per day in the window, INCLUDING DAYS WITH NO EVENTS — the series is pre-populated with zeros and then filled, so a flat zero run is genuinely quiet rather than missing data.

errorCode.description: The error code returned to the caller.

percentage.description: Share of all errors in the window, to 2dp. 0 when there were no errors.

rateLimit.description: The limit applied to this key.

callsInWindow.description: Calls made in the current window.

utilizationPercent.description: callsInWindow against rateLimit, to 2dp, CLAMPED AT 100 — a key that has been throttled well past its limit still reports exactly 100, so this cannot show how far over a caller is running.

grnRequired.description: The dispatch's customer has 'GRN required on delivery' set (crm.customers.grn_required).

courierWarning.description: A booking warning (e.g. unknown hub); cleared by a later booked callback without one.

courierErrorOpen.description: true when last_courier_error_at is set and courier_error_resolved_at is not — an unresolved courier error.

podSignedBy.description: PROOF OF DELIVERY. Non-null here is the signal that the goods were received — it is what an integration chasing delivery confirmation polls for.

grnNumber.description: The GRN on the dispatch — a manual GRN wins over the courier one.

grnRequired.description: The dispatch's customer has 'GRN required on delivery' set (crm.customers.grn_required).

courierWarning.description: A booking warning (e.g. unknown hub); cleared by a later booked callback without one.

deliveryAddress.description: The delivery address as dispatched to.

cartons.description: The cartons on the dispatch, with their barcodes.

courierStatus.description: booked → manifested → collected → in_transit → delivered. courier_status only moves forward; a lower or equal status is recorded but not applied. `failed` records an error and never changes the status.

errorMessage.description: The failure text, stored whole. `<Step>: <reason>` gives the step.

failedStep.description: The step that failed; otherwise parsed from the errorMessage prefix.

statusAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this event happened at the courier. Not stored in its own column — kept in the history row's payload (sales.dispatch_courier_events) and surfaced as courierStatusAt on the dispatch-notes list/detail for the dispatch's current status.

podSignedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the POD signature

hubCode.description: The courier hub the booking went to

courierWarning.description: A booking that needs a person to look (e.g. unknown hub). A later booked callback without it clears it.

grnNumber.description: The customer's GRN, when the driver captured it. A manual GRN is never overwritten.

courierStatus.description: The courier status as just received. See `applied` for whether it changed the dispatch's courier status.

applied.description: True when this callback moved the courier status forward. False for a lower or equal status (recorded, not applied) and always for `failed` (the error is recorded instead).

courierWarning.description: A booking warning (e.g. unknown hub); cleared by a later booked callback without one.

grnNumber.description: The GRN on the dispatch — a manual GRN wins over the courier one.

lastCourierError.description: The last courier error recorded (kept, marked resolved, after a forward status).

code.description: The customer account code. THE EXTERNAL IDENTIFIER — not the id.

branchId.description: The customer's operational branch (customers.branch_id) — null when none was given. This is NOT the entity: the customer always belongs to the key's entity regardless of this field. `?branchId=` filters on it, scoped within the entity.

branchId.description: The customer's operational branch (customers.branch_id) — null when none was given. This is NOT the entity: the customer always belongs to the key's entity regardless of this field. `?branchId=` filters on it, scoped within the entity.

creditBalance.description: The current balance on the account, as a numeric string. Detail only — the list omits it, so a client needing balances for a page of customers must fetch each one.

addressCode.description: The address code, unique within the customer.

gln.description: GS1 Global Location Number of the delivery point (13 digits), or null.

isDefault.description: Whether this is the default delivery address for the customer.

total.description: data.length — this list is UNPAGINATED, so total always equals the number of rows returned. It is not a count of a larger set.

data.description: Statement lines — invoices, credit notes and payments interleaved in date order. THERE IS NO OPENING BALANCE LINE: the statement starts from the transactions it returns, so a client summing these does not get the account balance unless the whole history is in range. The internal statement endpoint has the same gap; see docs/FINDING-customer-statement-opening-balance.md.

currency.description: The currency the lines are stated in.

stockCode.description: The stock code — the external identifier for a product.

costPrice.description: A numeric string. THE STANDING COST ON THE PRODUCT, not the warehouse weighted-average cost — an integration valuing stock from this field will not match the inventory valuation report, which uses WAC per warehouse.

stockCode.description: The stock code — the external identifier for a product.

costPrice.description: A numeric string. THE STANDING COST ON THE PRODUCT, not the warehouse weighted-average cost — an integration valuing stock from this field will not match the inventory valuation report, which uses WAC per warehouse.

sellingUom.description: The UOM the product sells in.

purchaseUom.description: The UOM the product is bought in.

isSerialTracked.description: TRUE MEANS EVERY MOVEMENT NEEDS SERIAL NUMBERS. An integration posting receipts or dispatches against a serial-tracked product without them will be rejected, so this is the field to read before building a posting payload.

stockCode.description: The product this barcode resolves to.

barcodeType.description: The barcode type's display name (e.g. 'Code 128'). Null for a legacy-column match — it carries no type.

uom.description: The unit THIS BARCODE represents (each / box / case …) — not necessarily the product's stocking unit.

conversionFactor.description: A numeric string. Restates `uom` in the product's stocking units.

stockingUom.description: The unit the product is stocked in.

isPrimary.description: Whether this is the primary barcode for its unit. Always true for a legacy-column match.

source.description: 'barcode' — resolved via the many-per-unit product_barcodes table (the same lookup the internal WMS scan uses). 'legacy' — the single products.barcode column, used only when no product_barcodes row matches; always factor 1 in the stocking unit.

totalOnHand.description: Physical stock across all warehouses, as a numeric string.

totalAvailable.description: On hand LESS reserved. This is the number to quote an availability from — on-hand includes stock already reserved against picks.

totalReserved.description: Reserved against picks. Reservation happens at pick, not at order.

totalOnOrder.description: On outstanding purchase orders — incoming, not yet received.

warehouses.description: The same four figures broken down per warehouse.

data.description: { code, name, symbol, decimalPlaces, isBaseCurrency }. EXACTLY ONE row should carry isBaseCurrency — it is the currency the GL reports in, and an integration converting amounts needs it to know which side of a rate it is on. No rates are returned here.

{ code, description, rate, taxType, isActive }. `rate` is a PERCENTAGE as a number, via `parseFloat(rate) || 0` — so a tax code with a null or unparseable rate is reported as 0, indistinguishable from a genuine zero-rated code. taxType defaults to the string 'VAT' when the column is null. Tax codes are GLOBAL, not entity-scoped, despite the entityId in the path.

{ code, description, termType, days, statementCutoffDay, fixedDayOfMonth, monthOffset, isActive }. TERMTYPE DECIDES WHICH OF THE OTHER FIELDS APPLY — a days-based term uses `days`, a statement term uses statementCutoffDay/fixedDayOfMonth/monthOffset. Computing a due date from `days` alone is wrong for statement terms.
{ code, description, isActive }. NO CONVERSION FACTORS — this is the flat UOM list, not the UOM groups that define each/box/pallet ratios, so it cannot be used to convert quantities.
The warehouses visible to this entity.
{ code, name, isActive, address, branchType }. Branches are ENTITIES in this schema — the id here is what customers report as `branchId`.
{ id, parentId, code, name }. A FLAT LIST OF A TREE — parentId is the only structure, so a client wanting the hierarchy assembles it. Root categories have parentId null.
